items.title: Theorem 3.1: sparse nonnegative identity-frame weights with exact two-sided Loewner bound
items.statement_scope: Suppose d > 1 (real) and v_1,...,v_m are vectors in R^n with Σ_{i≤m} v_i v_i^T = id_{R^n}. Then there exist scalars s_i ≥ 0 with |{i : s_i ≠ 0}| ≤ dn such that id_{R^n} ⪯ Σ_{i≤m} s_i v_i v_i^T ⪯ ((d+1+2√d)/(d+1−2√d)) id_{R^n}. Here A ⪯ B means B−A is positive semidefinite (author notation, journal.tex:349-350). The author's real d>1 hypothesis, arbitrary finite vector family, nonnegative scalars, support bound ≤dn, and exact two-sided ratio are retained without strengthening or rounding.

semantic_comparisons.title: Sparse Cuts for the Positive Semidefinite Cone
semantic_comparisons.basis: Exact supplied primary row: source0.tex:548-557, label lem:dnnform; the supplied extract states an SDP reformulation for a sparse-cut problem.
semantic_comparisons.comparison: No plausible semantic overlap. 196093 proves an equivalence/reformulation of a graph sparse-cut problem: min_C { C • Y_LP : C ⪰ 0, C_{ij} ≤ 0 for (i,j) not in E, ||diag(C)||_1 ≤ 1 }. The counted result is an existence theorem for nonnegative fractional weights over an arbitrary identity-sum family of rank-one projectors, with support ≤dn and an explicit two-sided Loewner condition-number bound. The objects (an SDP feasible cone versus a rank-one vector family), hypotheses (support/nonnegativity/diagonal ℓ1 constraint versus d>1 and Σ v_i v_i^T = I), and conclusions (problem equivalence versus weighted-selection existence) are all different.
